title: Adaptive by design
dek: A research team demonstrated an AI-powered worm that adapts its attack strategy to each target it encounters. The most important finding is not the worm itself. It is what the paper reveals about attacker adaptability, accessibility, and the economics of offensive capability.

title: Reading regulation like a threat model
dek: Auditors read a regulation for clauses to evidence. Researchers read a system for the assumptions that break it. This is what happens when you point the second habit at the first: faster gap analysis, sharper scoping, and controls that map to real exposure rather than to a checklist.

title: Understanding the criticality of securing our robots
dek: From Ancient Greek automata to connected surgical robots — why the safety of modern robotic systems has become a critical cybersecurity challenge, and where we need to start.

title: What side-channels taught me about assurance
dek: Systems leak in ways their designers never intended. So do compliance programmes. A look at the gap between what a control claims and what it actually emits.

title: Supply chain due diligence without the theatre
dek: Traditional third-party risk management was designed for a slower era. Why the operating assumptions behind vendor assurance have collapsed, and where the discipline is going.
